newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 15.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said yesterday that the package of economic measures, over which discussions have been held in the cabinet for two weeks, are 90 percent finished.

- Nervousness of domestic and foreign investors over the contents of the cabinet's measures to support the economy knocked the crown down below its basket parity for the first time since last year's parliamentary elections.
- Insurer Ceska Kooperativa bought 49.1 percent of shares of Sanatorium Astoria. The National Property Fund announced a minimum sale price in the public tender of 26 million crowns.
- According to Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, between 1993 and 1997, the government budget has given about 16 billion crowns to ore and coal mining.

- The owners of Prima Television could soon change. The American-European company SBS, Chemapol and the American company CME, which currently controls Nova Television, are all rumoured to be candidates for a stake in Prima.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to the Czech Statistical Bureau, agriculture sector sales decreased, year-on-year, by 4.1 percent in February, and by 0.6 percent for the first two months of 1997, year-on-year.
- Chemopetrol had gross profits of 522.5 million crowns and total sales of 4.6 billion crowns during the first quarter of this year.

PRAVO - Yesterday, in front of the council of the alliance in Brussels, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus confirmed the Czech Republic's intentions to concentrate its efforts on obtaining NATO membership. He met the same day with NATO General Secretary Javier Solana.

- Unisys and IBM CR sent a proposal to the administration for protecting economic tenders to begin reviewing a decision by Defense Minister Miloslav Vyborny to award EDS-Digital a contract for a military staff information system.
- The holding company Tabak agreed with Slovak International Tabak a.s. to cooperate in manufacturing cigarettes, and for importing Slovak tobacco to the Czech Republic.
- After Chemapol's recent share issue of 1.64 billion crowns, the main owner of Chemapol became bank IPB, which holds 14.68 percent of Chemapol's basic capital.
LIDOVE NOVINY - HSBC Investment Bank has decided to finish the sale of Agrobanka by this July, according to a representative of HSBC in London.
- Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec decided cut his visit to the United States short because of Wednesday's cabinet meeting. He met yesterday with the U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
- President Vaclav Havel will visit Bonn on April 24, and German President Roman Herzog will visit Prague on April 29. They should bring a close to the Czech-German Declaration.
